newsitem.title: EGYPT: Egyptian police arrest new militant group.
newsitem.headline: Egyptian police arrest new militant group.

text.p: Egyptian police in north Cairo have arrested 16 members of a militant Islamist group which planned to attack prominent people and senior policemen, government newspapers said on Sunday.
The group, which called itself the military wing of the Jihad organisation, was found in possession of large quantities of pamphlets, knives and other such weapons, they said.
The interior ministry's information centre said it had no information on the case.

"They are being questioned on charges of planning to commit terrorist operations against important people, leading policemen, writers, journalists and artists," said the government newspaper al-Gomhuria.
"They planned to restore the Jihad organisation after the recent arrest of many Jihad leaders. They confessed...to receiving finance from terrorist leaders abroad," it added.
Jihad was the organisation which assassinated Egyptian president Anwar Sadat in 1981. Another militant organisation, the Vanguards of Conquest, is also a revived version of Jihad.
Both are smaller than the Gama'a al-Islamiya (Islamic Group), the main organisation fighting to overthrow the government and make Egypt a strict Islamic state.
The newspapers said a state security prosecutor on Saturday ordered the men detained for questioning for 15 days.
